questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country where I was fluent in a language, so I could fully benefit from the experience. I have been to Australis before but I wanted to experience it as a resident and not just a tourist. Melbourne is very similar to Copenhagen culture with their huge coffee and food-scene, which ultimately drew me there

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KU is OK at providing the information needed, but you also need to stay alert to make sure there are not any deadlines you are missing. Going on exchange is a ton of ''paperwork''

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne had an office or ''spot 1'' if you needed information or help, also during your stay, with anything related to the university. The system in regards to applying for different courses was also easy to figure out. However UniMelb is so big that it can get a bit overwhelming - the amount of exchange and international students made the first week of orientation almost disorganized, even though they had put a lot of work into it

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I joined a FB group, that I had been recommended. I got my room at my first try, but I know it takes longer for others. Also, I started looking quite in advance (I flew in July and started looking in April, maybe?), while others look after they arrive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is waayyy cheaper and you get to connect with locals

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Described above

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot through UniMelb online, Orientation week and also Stop 1, the student office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I registrered for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a test period where you can go the different classes to see whether it is something for you. I ended up changing a few of them - so please take advantage of this opportunity!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that the level at UniMelb was pretty high in general. I could tell the level 1(2) classes were easier than the level 3.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more active - barely any lectures, a lot of seminars and presentations. The students carried the lectures a lot of the time

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Islam in the Modern World, Social Problems in Japan, Philosophical Issues: Race and Gender, Gender and Contemporary Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Social Problems in Japan was by far my favorite course! The professor was so enthausiastic and I learned so much during that course (I have previously studied Japanese studies, which was definitely a pro but you can easily follow the course with no previous knowledge to Japan or Japan language/culture)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The public transporation in Melbourne is fairly expensive - 5 AUD for a ride, 2.5 AUD if you get the student discount card. 
Also, travelling around Australia during my stay was more expensive than I thought

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Flights around Australia, public transportation. Rent is also more expensive than in Copenhagen I would say

Coffee and food is quite a lot cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sport-activities but also cultural clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not partake in any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Great Ocean Road weekend trip, Noosa, Byron etc 
Me and a couple of friends did a van trip around WA for 3 weeks, that was the most unique and unforgettable vacation I have ever done

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, Australian culture is basically just European culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The slang was more difficult that I could have imagined, that took me quite a while to get used to as they use it a lot A LOT

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness!! Unlike anything else, my favorite thing about Australia is for sure the people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is a great campus with a lot of good fascilities, use them - also take advantage of stop 1 if you need help. UniMelb might be a top university, but do not let that scare you. Do the assignments and you will be fine

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: GO, it was the best 7 months of my life. I loved UniMelb

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends (for life) and living abroad. Travelling around Australia.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period was quite tough, but not unbearable. (I find KU exams tougher)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
